The S3 object is created independently of the bucket's default server-side encryption configuration. If the object is uploaded first, it will not inherit the configured AES256 default encryption; make the object wait for the bucket encryption configuration.
The add-ons module already has an implicit dependency on this S3 object through the Spark History Server Helm configuration interpolation. Its explicit depends_on entry duplicates that dependency.
The managed node group directly references this IAM role in node_role_arn, which already establishes the dependency; the explicit depends_on entry is redundant.
The provisioner command interpolates this IAM role's ID, creating an implicit dependency already; the explicit depends_on entry is redundant.
The provisioner command interpolates this namespace's ID, creating an implicit dependency already; the explicit depends_on entry is redundant.
The Auto Scaling group already waits for the launch-template output, whose configuration depends on this instance profile. The explicit dependency is therefore transitively established and redundant.

The Auto Scaling group waits for the launch-template output, which depends on the instance profile and thus transitively on this IAM role. This explicit depends_on edge adds no ordering beyond the existing dependency chain.

The EBS CSI managed add-on uses the IRSA role ARN, but the dependency through the role output does not wait for the policy attachment to finish. The add-on may be created before its required EC2 permissions are attached; make it depend on the IRSA policy attachment.

The VPC CNI managed add-on receives the IRSA role ARN, but the role output does not ensure its policy attachments are complete before the add-on is created. Add an ordering dependency on the IRSA policy attachment so the CNI add-on does not start without its required permissions.
